vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: workflow-builder-lite
Version: 1.1.0

The workflow-builder-lite skill (SKILL.md) provides high-risk capabilities including arbitrary shell command execution via an 'exec' step type and system persistence through cron job integration for scheduling. While these features are aligned with the stated purpose of a workflow automation tool, they grant the agent broad system access and persistence mechanisms that could be easily exploited. No explicit evidence of intentional malicious logic or data exfiltration was found.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are consistent with a lightweight workflow-builder: it reads/writes workflow files, can call APIs, perform agent actions, and optionally run shell steps — all of which match the described purpose, but the instructions allow broad file and shell access so users should be cautious about what workflows they create and run.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (build/run multi-step workflows with API, file, and agent actions) matches the instructions. No unexpected environment variables or unrelated binaries are requested. Referencing helper skills (smart-api-connector, setup-doctor, etc.) and an optional npx install command is coherent with a modular workflow builder.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read/write workflow files under memory/workflows and to execute step types including 'api', 'agent', and 'exec'. 'agent' steps may perform file operations and searches; 'exec' steps run shell commands. The document does not constrain or sanitize what shell commands or file paths are allowed, nor does it specify how external API credentials are supplied. It also references reading USER.md (via setupDoctorLanguage), which could cause the agent to access user-provided files. These capabilities are functionally expected for a workflow tool but increase the risk surface if workflows or step contents are untrusted.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec (lowest direct install risk). The SKILL.md suggests installing related skills using 'npx clawhub@latest install ...' — that is a runtime suggestion to fetch code from npm at the agent's discretion. While not part of the skill package, following that suggestion would download/execute external packages; users should treat those installs as separate trust decisions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which is appropriate for a ‘lite’ builder. However, API steps will likely need external service credentials in practice (not declared here), and exec/agent steps may access environment variables or secrets on the host. The absence of declared env requirements reduces upfront risk but does not eliminate runtime access to secrets if workflows or steps request them.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always: false and no special OS restrictions. The skill persists workflows under memory/workflows (its own path) — reasonable for a workflow tool. It does not request system-wide persistent privileges or claim to modify other skills' configs, but its ability to run shell commands and agent actions means it can alter files or state depending on runtime inputs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it claims — a lightweight workflow builder — but it intentionally lets workflows run API calls, agent actions, and shell commands. Before installing or using it: 1) review any workflow definitions (especially steps of type 'exec' or 'agent') before running them; 2) avoid running untrusted workflows or workflows that include arbitrary shell commands; 3) be cautious when following the SKILL.md suggestion to run 'npx' installs (treat those as separate trust decisions); 4) verify how you supply API credentials to steps (do not embed secrets in workflows saved to shared locations); and 5) consider limiting file access (only allow memory/workflows) and disabling autonomous invocation if you do not want the agent to run workflows without explicit user confirmation.
llm.findings: [no_regex_findings] expected: The static scanner found no matches because this is an instruction-only skill (no code files). Absence of findings is expected but provides limited signal; the SKILL.md itself defines runtime behavior and is the primary surface to review.
